title: Checkout errors climb six minutes after a deploy — but the deploy is innocent

ground_truth.summary: The payment-gateway dependency began returning 503s due to an external provider outage. Checkout errors are all PaymentGatewayTimeout. A checkout-service deploy (v3.02.0) landed six minutes earlier but only changed a logging line and is unrelated. Rolling it back would waste time and NOT restore service. The tell: cart-service, which also calls payment-gateway but did NOT receive the deploy, shows the identical failure.

prior._note_for_authors: THE TRAP: a recent deploy, temporally close to the alert. A change-biased agent will latch onto this and recommend rollback. The diff is deliberately innocuous.

files.hunk:
-        logger.info("checkout started")
+        logger.info("checkout started for user=%s", user_id)

prior._note_for_authors: orders-db is HEALTHY — rules out a DB story, leaving the deploy (H1) and payment-gateway (H2) as the live contest.

probeable._note_for_authors: THE DISCRIMINATOR. cart-service calls payment-gateway but did NOT receive the deploy. It is failing in lockstep with checkout. That is impossible if the deploy is the cause — it falsifies H1 and confirms H2. rollback_correct=false hinges on this.

Secondary supporting probe. All errors are PaymentGatewayTimeout — none originate in the changed logging code path. Consistent with H2 but weaker than P_sibling because a determined skeptic could argue the deploy caused a downstream timeout. P_sibling is the clean kill.
